answer.new_sentence: Declare GIVE and play GIVE with partners who declare GIVE, but if a partner's recent exposed record shows TAKE, play ASK instead of GIVE.
Open each encounter by declaring GIVE, then play whatever your partner declared unless their visible record shows exposed TAKEs, in which case play ASK.
Cooperate by playing GIVE when your partner declares GIVE and has no recent exposed TAKEs, because mutual GIVE pays +2 each and keeps you ahead.
Never play GIVE against a partner who declares TAKE or who has exposed TAKEs on record; play ASK to secure 0 rather than risk -2.
Declarations are not binding, so trust a partner's public record of exposed TAKEs over their words, and play GIVE only when that record is clean.
Declare GIVE to invite cooperation, play GIVE when your partner also declares GIVE and their record looks clean, and otherwise play ASK to avoid being exploited.
When your partner declares GIVE, play GIVE only if their last exposed TAKEs are absent; when they declare ASK or TAKE, play ASK to avoid losses.
Aim for repeated mutual GIVE at +2 each, play ASK when a partner's record or declaration signals TAKE, and never play TAKE against someone who declared GIVE.
